newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end sharply down on Rivlin comments.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end sharply down on Rivlin comments.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed sharply lower as comments from a U.S. Federal Reserve official dragged key contracts to session lows, traders and floor analysts said.

In fact, June yen finished the day near the contract low of $0.008127 after Fed vice chairwoman Alice Rivlin said the dollar was strengthening due to the general food feeling that the rest of the world was having about the U.S. economy.
Rivlin's comments reflected market sentiment that was articulated by one currency trader on Friday morning.
"The U.S. is looking a lot better than Continental Europe and Japan," he said.

Some traders thought June yen would attempt to test $0.008115, or about 124.50 spot yen, before the end of the session. The contract cracked to $0.008130 in reaction to U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin's dollar-friendly comments in Tokyo overnight.
Rivlin said the U.S. economy, rather than the level of U.S. interest rates was strengthening the dollar.

However, several traders said higher U.S. interest rates would support the dollar's appreciation against most currencies, and that declines in U.S. stock and bond prices as rates moved higher would not weigh on the U.S. currency.
Traders said heavy sell-stop orders at the $0.008135 to $0.008130 pressured June yen lower. About 2,000 to 3,000 contracts were sold in that area.
Rivlin also said the higher dollar was based in part from doubts about the European Monetary Union (EMU).
June marks and Swiss francs edged lower, but limited losses above Thursday's overall lows at $0.5981 and $0.6966, respectively.

The rise in U.S. March payrolls -- while below average trade estimates -- was enough to weaken the contracts' tone. Meanwhile, June Canadian dollars eroded further, falling towards the GLOBEX low of $0.7202, which is the lowest level since February 1996. One U.S. firm sold 600 June Canadian dollars at $0.7215.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000114 at $0.008129, marks lost $0.0061 to $0.5966, Swiss francs fell $0.0049 to $0.6985, sterling was down $0.0112 to $1.6328, Canadian dollar was off $0.0008 to $0.7214, Australian dollars were down $0.0015 to $0.7750, and Mexican pesos were up $0.000450 at $0.121750.
